name: Nyong
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Kouonang (épouse Nganmou), Alise. 1983. Esquisse phonologique du parler bali-kumbat. Mémoire de Maîtrise en Linguistique, Dép. des Langues Africaines et Linguistique, Université de Yaoundé (année 1982-1983). 105 pp. [MPG PuRe Language Description Heritage item_403423, PUBLIC PDF]
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2.2 'Les unités suprasegmentales : les tonèmes' (pp. 76-81) treats only tone: Bali-Kumbat 'est donc un parler à tons', three level tonemes H/M/L plus rising and falling; TOC (pp. 102-105), Notes préliminaires (syllable/morpheme structure, pp. 22-26) and Résumé (pp. 82-84) checked — no mention of accent/stress anywhere.

sources.citation: Zheltov, Alexander. 2020. Plurality marking in Leko and Yendang groups (Adamawa, Niger-Congo) with some reference to noun classification. Language in Africa 1(3): 125-154. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-125-154
sources.note: Nothing; states the Nyong data are preliminary, 'still more phonetic than phonological, the tonal notation needs to be specified' (p.129-130) and fn.15 'The tonal notation is very preliminary. The absence of tone marking indicates middle tone.'

sources.citation: Zheltov, A. Ju. 2014. Elementy morfosintaksisa jazyka n'ong (adamaua, niger-kongo). In V.F. Vydrin & A.Ju. Zheltov (eds), Antropologija i lingvistika: Materialy peterburgskix èkspedicij v Afriku, 156-167. SPb: MAE RAN.
sources.note: Nothing; morphosyntax only (number, adjectives, pronouns, logophoricity, ditransitives) on Nigerian Nyong; tones marked on examples with a footnote that some tones are unchecked.

sources.citation: Zheltov, A.Ju. 2013. [Adamawa languages: 100-word lists and lexicostatistics note incl. Nyong] in Afrikanskij sbornik 2013 (SPb: MAE RAN), and Afrikanskij sbornik 2009/2011/2015/2017 full texts grepped for n'ong
sources.note: Nothing; only lexicostatistic percentages involving Nyong.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory PH 1181 'Bali-Kumbat' (language Nyong, nyon1241), source Kouonang 1983
sources.note: Segment and tone inventory only (42 segments incl. tones); no stress information.
Lists vowels, consonants and 'five tones: high, mid, low, rising, and falling'; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, U. Adamawa Languages Project (Mainz), Samba-Duru group page
sources.note: Only notes that Mubaako (Məbaako, Nyong) is spoken around Balikumbat; no linguistic data.

sources.citation: Zheltov, Alexander (in prep./forthcoming). Fuller description of Nigerian Nyong (Mumbake) phonology from the 2012-2014 Yola field trips (St Petersburg State University / MAE RAN Adamawa project).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Zheltov 2020 calls his Nyong data 'the first documentation' and says transcription/tone are unresolved; any later phonology paper by him (Language in Africa, Afrikanskij sbornik) would be the first place a stress/accent statement for Nyong could appear.

sources.citation: Simo, Michel. 1979. Esquisse linguistique du Bali Kumbat. Mémoire (maîtrise), Université de Yaoundé.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only other description of the Bali-Kumbat (Mubako) variety listed by Glottolog; a general 'esquisse linguistique' may contain a prosody remark that Kouonang's tone-only sketch lacks.

sources.citation: Fabre, Gwenaëlle. 2003. Étude du samba leko, parler d'Allani (Cameroun du Nord, famille Adamawa). Thèse de doctorat, Université Paris III (published LINCOM 2004); and Noss, Philip. 1976. Samba Leeko: outline of phonology. Yaoundé: SIL.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Closest described relative (Samba Leko, samb1305 — a different glottocode); Kouonang treats Bali-Kumbat as a Samba Leko 'parler'. Would show whether the Leko group is described with any accent alongside tone, but cannot stand in for nyon1241.

sources.citation: Griffin, Margaret A. 1994. A rapid appraisal survey of Mubako (ALCAM 300 Samba leekɔ). Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon.

sources.note: SIL RA survey of the Cameroonian enclave; unlikely to state stress but may contain a phonological note or point to unpublished SIL phonology/orthography work on Mubako.
